question: The audit trusts 463 of 1947 lifts, 24%. On the other 76% the engine declines to opine, so those harnesses can never produce a finding. WHY are they untrusted, and which cause is worth fixing?

two_hypotheses_that_were_WRONG.libc_and_local_noise: The top missed names are getpid, memcmp, read, __builtin_trap, _cleanup_, and harness-local helpers, which looked like the lifter penalising itself for calls it correctly ignores. Measured: only 9% of missed calls. 88% are GENUINE EXTERNAL CALLS.
two_hypotheses_that_were_WRONG.fuzzeddataprovider_plumbing: The dominant shape is member calls, and the first example was `stream.PickValueInArray(..)` -- harness plumbing rather than a library call. Measured across all receivers: `fdp` accounts for 60 of 2726. The rest are real library objects -- codec, db, parser, doc, options, phone_util.

THE_ANSWER: The gap is not a bug. It is a C lifter meeting C++ class-API harnesses. The untrusted verdict on those is CORRECT -- the engine cannot model `codec.decode(data, size)` and says so rather than guessing.
what_this_licenses: Building a member-call lift path is the single largest available increase in audit reach, and audit reach is what produced the one merged upstream fix. A receiver is a resource and a method is an op; the IR already expresses both.
what_it_does_NOT_license: Any expectation that 201 more trusted lifts yield 201 more findings. The current rate is 2 real defects in 463 trusted lifts. The honest projection is under one additional finding, and the case for doing it is compounding reach rather than a forecast.

OUTCOME_member_call_lifting.built: A receiver declared as a C++ object is a resource; a method on it is an op. Constructors lift as a create named for the TYPE. std and FuzzedDataProvider receivers stay excluded as plumbing.
OUTCOME_member_call_lifting.why_the_projection_was_optimistic: The census asked which lifts had NO cause other than member calls. That is the right question for an upper bound and the wrong one for a forecast: lifting the member calls exposes causes that were underneath them. simdjson and clickhouse became readable at the call level and immediately failed on unbound uses of `Data`/`Size` -- a different defect that the member-call barrier had been hiding.
OUTCOME_member_call_lifting.false_positives: still 0. 489 trusted lifts, 2 blocking verdicts, both correct.
OUTCOME_member_call_lifting.what_it_is_worth: +26 trusted lifts is real and permanent, and the ceiling is not reached: the 181 mixed cases and the newly exposed taint failures are now the next layer. But it is not the +43% the census suggested and that number should not be repeated.

OUTCOME_taint_through_fields.census: After member-call lifting, 539 lifts failed on unbound uses of data/size ALONE, and 419 of those were short by EXACTLY ONE occurrence.

the_wrong_fix_and_what_it_cost.idea: An alias assignment `const uint8_t *data2 = data;` consumes an occurrence of `data` that can never become a bound argument, because the ALIAS is what later calls take. Subtracting those from the counter looked like correcting an accounting error.
the_wrong_fix_and_what_it_cost.why_it_was_wrong: The counter was doing its job. It reports that a flow was not followed, and the flows really were not followed -- h3 casts the input to a struct and passes `args->index`, which the lifter never bound. Silencing the counter turned 'we cannot read this' into 'we read it and the harness is broken': 13 false S5.INPUT_NOT_CONSUMED verdicts against harnesses that consume input fine.

OUTCOME_taint_through_fields.the_right_fix: Follow the flow instead. A field of a tainted object is tainted, so `args->index` carries the input. The counter then balances by itself.
OUTCOME_taint_through_fields.the_trade_stated_plainly: The wrong fix bought +55 trusted lifts by manufacturing 17 false accusations against correct harnesses. The right fix bought +7 with none. +7 is the honest number.
OUTCOME_taint_through_fields.what_is_still_unread: h3 remains untrusted, and correctly: `H3_EXPORT(cellToLatLng)(args->index, &geo)` is a MACRO-GENERATED CALL, a blind spot the field-taint fix does not touch. That is the next shape, not this one.

STOPPING_POINT.why_stop: The remaining causes are a LONG TAIL. Among the 419 lifts short by exactly one occurrence, the most common syntactic skeleton appears 10 times; the next appears 7. There is no dominant shape left to fix, so each further fix buys a handful of lifts rather than a tier.
STOPPING_POINT.macro_calls_were_checked_and_rejected: H3_EXPORT(fn)(args) looked like the next lever after it kept h3 untrusted. Measured: 19 lifts across two macro families. Sized before building, and not built.
STOPPING_POINT.the_lesson_that_cost_the_most: Two projections in one session were far too optimistic -- 201 member-call lifts became 26, and an alias-counter 'fix' promising +55 delivered 17 false positives instead. A census that asks 'which lifts have NO other cause' gives an upper bound, and fixing one layer exposes the next. Upper bounds should be labelled as such the moment they are computed.
STOPPING_POINT.recommendation: The compounding value of audit reach is real -- it produced the one merged upstream fix -- but it is no longer the cheapest source of it. Move to the GUI track, which is the weakest asset this project owns and is newly unblocked by a Linux host with Xvfb.
